cards.objective: Build a first monthly budget from real income and fixed costs.
cards.title: A budget planner that does the arithmetic for you
cards.summary: A free budgeting tool from the UK government-backed money guidance service. It walks through income, fixed costs and spending, then shows what is left and where it goes. It is general information rather than advice about your own circumstances.
takeaways: Writing fixed costs down is what makes them negotiable.
A budget is a plan for money you have, not a prediction of money you might get.

cards.objective: Understand how machine-learning models are trained and evaluated.

cards.summary: A free, self-paced course that introduces how machine learning models are trained and evaluated, with short videos and exercises rather than mathematics for its own sake. It is aimed at people who write software or work alongside those who do.
takeaways: Training a model means adjusting it until its predictions match known answers closely enough.
Most of the work in practice is preparing data, not choosing an algorithm.

cards.objective: Take the few security steps that prevent most ordinary attacks.
cards.title: The handful of security steps that matter most
cards.summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre's short guidance on protecting everyday accounts. It is deliberately a small number of steps, chosen because they prevent the majority of ordinary attacks, rather than an exhaustive list nobody follows.
takeaways: Protecting the email account that can reset every other password matters most.
Two-factor authentication blocks most attacks that start with a stolen password.

cards.objective: Apply evidence-led basics that help with getting to sleep.
cards.title: What actually helps when you cannot sleep
cards.summary: NHS guidance on sleep: regular timing, winding down, and when poor sleep is worth seeing a doctor about. It is short, free of supplements and gadgets, and clear about the point at which self-help is not the answer. General information, not medical advice.
takeaways: A consistent wake time does more for sleep than a consistent bedtime.
Persistent sleep problems are worth raising with a doctor rather than managing alone.

cards.objective: Use spaced review to remember what you learn for longer.
cards.title: Why reviewing at increasing intervals works
cards.summary: A long essay on using spaced repetition seriously: how review schedules affect what is retained, what makes a good prompt, and where the method stops helping. It is considerably more thoughtful than the usual flashcard advice, and honest about the effort involved.
takeaways: Reviewing just before you would have forgotten is what strengthens memory.
A good prompt asks for one specific thing, not a whole topic at once.
cards.nextStep: Turn one thing you learned this week into a single question and answer.

cards.objective: Read the primary evidence behind a warming climate.
cards.title: The evidence for a changing climate, from the primary source
cards.summary: NASA's plain summary of the physical evidence for climate change: temperature records, sea level, ice and the measurements behind them. It links to the underlying datasets, so a reader can check the claims rather than take them on trust.
takeaways: The clearest evidence is a long record of measurements, not any single hot year.
Primary datasets are published, so the headline claims can be checked directly.
cards.nextStep: Open one of the linked datasets and read what it actually measures.
